themes_detail.label: Food Safety Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 3.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 107% increase (z-score: 3.26)—suggesting potential health code violations or a cluster of problematic venues in Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights requiring immediate inspection and investigation.
evidence: 7 food establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.4 per week average (prior 8 weeks)
Represents 107% spike with z-score of 3.26 (statistically significant)
No recent Reddit discussions or local news coverage, suggesting emerging and unreported issue
reporting_angles: Which restaurants/food vendors are generating complaints and what violations are cited?
Are complaints concentrated in one area (5th Ave restaurant row?) or distributed across the district?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Density Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Homelessness visibility jumped 515% last week with 10 encampment complaints versus a baseline of 1.6 per week over 8 weeks (z-score: 4.49)—concurrent with CB budget requests for homeless services—indicating a rapid spike requiring urgent outreach and shelter coordination.
evidence: 10 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 per week average (prior 8 weeks)—515% increase
Z-score of 4.49 indicates extremely rare statistical event
Community Board has standing budget request for DHS homeless services, suggesting prior unmet need
reporting_angles: Where are encampments concentrated—waterfront parks, residential blocks, commercial corridors?
Are residents reporting safety concerns or sanitation issues alongside encampments?
Has DHS capacity or outreach activity changed recently; are existing services insufficient?

themes_detail.label: Electrical Infrastructure Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints exploded 860% two weeks ago, with 6 complaints versus a baseline of 0.6 per week (z-score: 6.27, highest severity)—an extreme anomaly suggesting downed lines, aging grid issues, or a specific infrastructure incident that warrants Con Edison and DOE investigation.
evidence: 6 electrical complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 per week average (prior 8 weeks)—860% increase
Highest z-score recorded (6.27), indicating most extreme outlier in dataset
Community Board has ongoing capital requests for DOB, consistent with infrastructure aging concerns
reporting_angles: Was there a specific storm, outage, or infrastructure failure two weeks ago that triggered complaints?
Are complaints concentrated in one neighborhood block or grid section?
Con Edison response times and whether residents are reporting repeated power issues in same locations

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped 400% last week to 5 complaints from a baseline of 1.0 per week (z-score: 4.0), alongside a 256% spike in obstruction complaints—suggesting streets are becoming increasingly blocked by discarded bikes, creating accessibility and sanitation hazards.
evidence: 5 abandoned bike complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 per week average (prior 8 weeks)—400% increase
Coincident 256% spike in obstruction complaints (8 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.2 avg)—z-score 3.68
Combined signal suggests systemic street clutter issue affecting pedestrian and wheelchair access
reporting_angles: Are abandoned bikes concentrated near bike-share stations (Citi Bike hubs) or scattered throughout district?
Sanitation Department removal protocols—how quickly are reported bikes cleared?
Are bike-share companies responsible for maintenance, or is city responsible for street cleanup?

themes_detail.label: Door/Window Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Door and window damage complaints spiked 182% three weeks ago to 19 complaints versus a baseline of 6.8 per week (z-score: 3.41)—potentially indicating break-ins, vandalism, or storm damage affecting residential security and suggesting a crime or weather pattern worth investigating.
evidence: 19 door/window complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 6.8 per week average (prior 8 weeks)—182% increase
Z-score of 3.41 indicates statistically significant spike
Timing suggests possible weather event (snow/ice storm) or uptick in break-ins requiring NYPD analysis
reporting_angles: NYPD crime data: were burglaries or attempted break-ins elevated three weeks ago?
Was there a significant weather event (nor'easter?) that caused wind/storm damage to buildings?
Interview residents about security concerns or recent incidents in their buildings or blocks
